Strong homology to reviewed GlmU proteins: 51.4–53.0% identity across 96.9–99.1% of the sequence.
Likely catalyzes both glucosamine-1-phosphate N-acetyltransferase and UDP-N-acetylglucosamine diphosphorylase reactions.

source_tools.relevance: Sequence analysis, Pfam domains, homology, and functional annotation

entities.name: GlmU
observations: Curated bacterial GlmU homologs catalyze the final two steps of UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis.
The C-terminal domain transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to glucosamine-1-phosphate.
The N-terminal domain converts N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate plus UTP into UDP-N-acetylglucosamine and pyrophosphate.
Curated homologs bind Mg2+ and form homotrimers; localization is cytoplasmic.
Associated processes include UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis, peptidoglycan biosynthesis, and lipid A biosynthesis.

entities.name: Peptidoglycan biosynthesis

entities.name: Lipid A biosynthesis
observations: In Gram-negative bacteria, UDP-GlcNAc produced by GlmU feeds lipid A and lipopolysaccharide biogenesis.
